publisher: National Tax Agency (国税庁, NTA), Japan
raw_extract:
〔税額の計算〕

(1) 月額表甲欄の使用例（給与所得者の扶養控除等申告書の提出がある場合）
（設例）
イ 給与等の支給額（月額）  420,000円
ロ 給与等から控除する社会保険料等  63,400円
ハ 扶養親族等の数  2人
   （源泉控除対象配偶者あり、源泉控除対象親族1人）

〔税額の計算〕
(1) 社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額を求めると、356,600円（420,000円−63,400円）となります。
(2) 月額表の「その月の社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額」欄で、356,600円が含まれる「356,000円以上359,000円未満」の行を求め、その行と「甲」欄の「扶養親族等の数 2 人」の欄との交わるところに記載されている金額7,020円を求めます。これがその給与等から源泉徴収をする税額です。

[Table (三) (290,000円〜439,999円) as printed on the same page, header: その月の社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額 | 甲 扶養親族等の数 0人 1人 2人 3人 4人 5人 6人 7人以上 | 乙 未満 税額]
356,000  359,000  12,220  9,000  7,020  5,410  3,800  2,170  560  0  71,900

[And the NTA's rule for employees who have NOT submitted a 扶養控除等申告書, printed as the 月額表乙欄 usage example on the next page]
(2) 月額表乙欄の使用例（給与所得者の扶養控除等申告書の提出がない場合）
（設例）
イ 給与等の支給額（月額）  80,750円
ロ 給与等から控除する社会保険料等  なし
〔税額の計算〕
(1) 給与等から控除する社会保険料等がありませんので、支給額80,750円がそのまま社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額になります。
(2) 月額表の「その月の社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額」欄で、80,750円が含まれる「105,000円未満」の行を求め、その行の「乙」欄を見ますと「その月の社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額の3.063％に相当する金額」となっています。したがって、2,473円（80,750円×3.063％、1円未満の端数は切り捨てます。）がその給与等から源泉徴収をする税額です。

supporting_sources.role: the actual 源泉徴収税額表 (monthly table) rows used in the derivation
the NTA's own instruction on what salary the table is applied to
supporting_sources.raw_extract: 2 税額表の使い方 … (1) 税額表に当てはめる給与等の金額は、その月（日）分の給与等の金額から厚生年金保険料、健康保険料及び雇用保険料などの社会保険料等を控除した後の金額によります。

derivation.method: DERIVED from the National Tax Agency's own 令和8年分 源泉徴収税額表. The gross input AND the social insurance input are both the NTA's OWN published worked-example figures, so no figure in claim jp-net-monthly-001 is mine. No percentage-of-gross guess was used.
derivation.step_1_source: NTA worked example: イ 給与等の支給額（月額） 420,000円
derivation.step_2_source: NTA worked example: ロ 給与等から控除する社会保険料等 63,400円
derivation.step_4_working: Row '356,000円以上359,000円未満' of table (三), column 甲 '扶養親族等の数 0人' = 12,220円. The NTA's own example reads 0-dependants off the same row as 12,220.
derivation.step_5b_working: 420,000 - 63,400 - 7,020 = JPY 349,580, which is the NTA's OWN worked example (its example employee has 2 dependants, so it reads 7,020 off the same row). Recorded to show the range the NTA itself documents.

graduate_salary_derivation.gross_source: MEXT-published 大卒初任給, see 010_gross_monthly_income.json in this directory
graduate_salary_derivation.social_insurance_status: NOT DERIVED - see notes and evidence_limitations. I could not source a primary-source monthly employee social insurance figure for a JPY 220,000 salary within this pass.
graduate_salary_derivation.what_IS_published: The NTA table rows for this band. If monthly social insurance were S, the salary after social insurance is 220,000 - S, and the tax is read off the row containing that number, column 甲 0人. For example at S = 33,220 (which is the NTA's own 15.095% ratio of social insurance to gross, from 63,400 / 420,000, applied to 220,000 - NOTE: this ratio is MY inference, not a published Japanese rate), the salary after social insurance is 186,780, the applicable row is '185,000円以上187,000円未満', the tax is 3,840, and the net is 220,000 - 33,220 - 3,840 = JPY 182,940.

claims.statement: DERIVED take-home pay in Japan, tax year Reiwa 8 (2026), for a single employee with no 扶養親族等 (no dependants) who is paid JPY 420,000 gross per month: JPY 420,000 gross less JPY 63,400 of employee social insurance less JPY 12,220 of 源泉徴収税額, giving JPY 344,380 net per month. All three inputs are the National Tax Agency's own published figures: the gross and the social insurance amount are the NTA's own 令和8年分 worked example, and the tax is the NTA's own table row 356,000円以上359,000円未満, 甲 0人 = 12,220. This is a NET figure, not gross.

The same JPY 420,000 gross and JPY 63,400 social insurance, but with the NTA's own worked-example tax of JPY 7,020 (its example employee has 扶養親族等の数 2人), giving JPY 349,580 net per month. This is the figure the NTA itself documents end to end, so it is the most directly verifiable number in this artifact, but it applies to an employee with two dependants, not a new graduate.

claims.unit: JPY per month (income tax withheld only)
claims.statement: The tax-only component at a graduate salary band, read directly from the NTA 令和8年分 月額表 (一): for a salary after social insurance in the band 185,000円以上187,000円未満, with 扶養親族等の数 0人, the 源泉徴収税額 is 3,840円 per month. This is INCOME TAX ONLY, not take-home, and it is not a net figure. The corresponding rows for this band are 187,000-189,000 = 3,910; 189,000-191,000 = 3,980; 191,000-193,000 = 4,050; 193,000-195,000 = 4,120.

claims.unit: percent of salary after social insurance
claims.statement: The NTA's 乙欄 rule: where a 給与所得者の扶養控除等申告書 has NOT been submitted, the 源泉徴収税額 is 'その月の社会保険料等控除後の給与等の金額の3.063％に相当する金額'. The NTA's own worked example: '80,750円×3.063％' = 2,473円. Recorded because it is a clean, fully published percentage rule, but note it is a flat rule for employees without the declaration form, not the rule for a typical new graduate who does submit it.

assumptions: TAX YEAR 令和8年分 (Reiwa 8 = 2026) for the 源泉徴収税額表.

扶養親族等の数 0人 (no dependants) for claims jp-net-monthly-001 and jp-net-monthly-003. This is the right assumption for a new graduate and is the single biggest lever on Japanese net pay: the same table row gives 9,000 at 1 person, 7,020 at 2 and 5,410 at 3.
甲欄 (the employee HAS submitted the 給与所得者の扶養控除等申告書). The 乙欄 flat 3.063% rule in claim jp-net-monthly-004 is a different situation and is recorded separately, not blended into the headline.
Employee is a 居住者 (resident), ordinary monthly salary, no 賞与 in the month, no pretax deduction such as 源泉徴収税額控除制度 (the non-taxable coffee-and-meals allowance) or similar treatment.

The social insurance figure of JPY 63,400 is the NTA's OWN published figure for its own JPY 420,000 example. It is NOT a social insurance rate I invented, and it is NOT a rate applicable to a graduate salary. The NTA explicitly states the table is keyed on 'its amount after deducting social insurance such as employee pension, health and employment insurance'.
notes: Claim jp-net-monthly-001 (JPY 344,380) is a genuine NET figure: gross less employee social insurance less withheld income tax, with all three inputs published by the National Tax Agency itself. The serious caveat is the SALARY LEVEL, not the method. JPY 420,000 per month is roughly twice a new graduate's salary; it is a mid-career figure. A Japanese new graduate earns about JPY 220,000 gross per month (see 010_gross_monthly_income.json in this directory, MEXT-published 大卒初任給), and the NTA's own table shows the tax component at that band is only JPY 3,840-4,120 per month - but the social insurance deduction still has to come out first, and THAT is the part I could not source. Japanese employee social insurance is not a single national rate: the 厚生年金保険料 depends on the 標準報酬月額 grade and is published per grade by the Japan Pension Service, the 健康保険 and 介護保険料 rates are set per health insurance association or per prefecture (協会けんぽ publishes different rates for every prefecture, and 健康保険組合 set their own), and 雇用保険料 is a separate published rate. There is therefore no single national 'social insurance' figure to quote for a graduate, and I refused to invent one. The JPY 182,940 figure in derivation.graduate_salary_derivation is therefore NOT a source figure: it depends on a 15.095% social insurance ratio that I inferred from the NTA's own mid-career example, and it is recorded only so that a reader with a real payslip can substitute the real number. Second caveat: the 扶養控除等申告書 in Japan is submitted once a year, usually in February, so a new graduate's first few months are often taxed in the 乙欄 way or with a partial 扶養 count, meaning first-year Japanese take-home is volatile and can be lower than a steady-state figure.
evidence_limitations: Population covered: a hypothetical Japanese salaried employee whose published worked-example salary is JPY 420,000 gross per month, single, no dependants, resident, submitting the 扶養控除等申告書. This is NOT a measured Japanese graduate salary and NOT a measured Japanese graduate take-home. No Japanese official source publishes a graduate take-home median. The JPY 420,000 salary in the NTA's own example is roughly double a new graduate's starting salary, so JPY 344,380 is a mid-career net and a new graduate's net would be substantially lower - but lower by how much cannot be stated here without a sourced social insurance figure, which I do not have. Regional variation is material in Japan: health and nursing care insurance rates are set per health insurance association and per prefecture, so a graduate in one prefecture or a company with a large 健康保険組合 takes home more than one with a small prefecture association at the same gross. Bonuses also matter for annual net but not for this monthly figure. A reader would be badly misled by using claim jp-net-monthly-003 (JPY 3,840) as take-home, or by treating JPY 344,380 as a graduate salary.
attempted_sources_not_used: https://www.nenkin.go.jp/service/kounen/hokenryo/ryogaku/ryogakuhyo/20200825.files/R07ryougaku.pdf (Japan Pension Service 厚生年金保険料額表, 令和7年度版) - located and confirmed to publish the per-grade 標準報酬月額 and the employee '折半額' at 9.150%, which would allow the pension component to be computed for JPY 220,000, but I did not read the specific grade row within this pass, so no figure from it is claimed here.

Japan Pension Service (日本年金機構) 厚生年金保険料額表 index page notes that from April 2026 (令和8年4月) a 子ども・子育て支援金 (childcare support contribution) regime is created and a contribution starts to be levied on top of medical insurance, income-dependent. I could not quantify it from a primary source within this pass, so the JPY 344,380 derivation may overstate net for a 2026 month, and the social insurance input is the least durable number in this artifact.
MHLW (厚生労働省) Annual Report on Labour / 毎月勤労統計調査 - not used: neither publishes a graduate-specific gross or net figure.
